messages:
nina.sales: Quick heads-upPOC with Orion Systems: they're seeing a spike of events in our console with null trace_ids and the forwarder logs show 403 -> 429 in quick succession. Customer worried data is lost.
aditya.ops: Can you paste the forwarder logs and one example event?
nina.sales: Pasted (sanitized):
```
2026-06-10T21:34:01Z INFO forwarder starting batch=8 size=2.3MB
2026-06-10T21:34:02Z ERROR upload failed status=403 err="AccessDenied: PutObject" attempt=0
2026-06-10T21:34:02Z INFO assume-role arn:aws:iam::777777777777:role/orion-forwarder session=900
2026-06-10T21:34:03Z INFO retrying upload attempt=1
2026-06-10T21:34:05Z ERROR upload failed status=429 err="TooManyRequests" attempt=1
```
Sample event: `{ "ts":"2026-06-10T21:34:01Z", "msg":"http request", "trace_id":null }`
zane.eng: Pattern looks like a short STS session (900s) -> role refresh mid-batch -> S3 PutObject denied for that slice -> ingest throttle for retries -> metadata and body get out of sync so trace mapping drops.
aditya.ops: Short customer-friendly line?
nina.sales: "This is due to short STS sessions causing mid-batch credential rotation; increase the role sessionDuration and allow PutObject on the upload prefix. Quick workaround: enable atomic/local buffering or reduce batch_size."
mira-support: Config suggestions to send them (YAML):
```
forwarder:
  buffer_mode: atomic
  s3_prefix: "orion/poc/%{env}/"
  aws_sts_session_duration: 21600
  max_batch_size_mb: 1.0
  retry:
    max_attempts: 4
```
zane.eng: Additional options if they can't change AWS role: 1) use our signed-upload proxy (signed URLs) so no role assumption on the forwarder, 2) enable multipart commit semantics on forwarder (feature-flag), or 3) route through our KMS upload-proxy (enterprise). Signed-URL proxy avoids rotation issues but requires short-lived upload tokens from our control plane.
aditya.ops: Also note: reducing batch size avoids crossing the rotation window and reduces chance of mid-batch refresh. That helped two other customers.
nina.sales: Customer asked whether the 429s are entirely our throttle.
aditya.ops: Yes the 429s are ingest-side rate limits on trial accounts; we can grant a small temporary burst if needed.
infra-bot: [quota] Temporary ingest burst applied org=orion-900 ttl=2h by aditya.ops :white_check_mark:
mira-support: If you want a one-line SRE blurb: "Increase STS sessionDuration and give PutObject to forwarder prefix; or enable atomic buffering/reduce batch size to avoid mid-batch credential refresh."
zane.eng: Follow-ups: 1) ops to run a dedup/consistency scan for the periods with buffering turned on 2) eng to add a detection rule for "mid-batch STS refresh" to surface clearer error messages (suggestion: surface `needs-role-refresh` vs `ingest-throttle` hints) 3) sales to add short KB snippet to POC playbook.
aditya.ops: I'll run the dedup scan and post results within 30m.
infra-bot: [deploy] forwarder v1.15.0 -> canary started 2026-06-10T21:40:00Z :rocket:
nina.sales: Orion applied the config; they increased STS sessionDuration to 21600 and switched to atomic buffering. They retried and report trace_ids visible again for last 4 batches.
mira-support: Great I'll follow up with the KB and send the snippet + one-liner to their SRE. :thumbsup:
aditya.ops: Dedup scan: 0 duplicates found for the affected window, buffering committed atomically as expected. Posting result now.
zane.eng: Thanks everyone. Let's add signed-URL instructions to the KB as a fallback for customers who can't modify IAM.
nina.sales: Closing loop with the customer and updating the POC checklist. Thanks all!
